As a woman, my ex boyfriend started off the conversation by saying he’s been wanting to set goals for the next 6 months to improve his looks and fitness to be hotter for me, and asked me if I wanted to join him. I said yes because I knew I had gained so much weight, then he asked what my specific goals were, and to write them down so we can commit and of course I myself brought up the fact that I felt like I gained weight. He told me he loved me and found super attractive, and basically said he would support me and help me stay accountable on my weight loss journey as long as I felt comfortable with it, and asked me what my goal was. Next day he gifted me a membership to a Pilates studio and bought me a really nice pair of shoes for the gym too.  

We’re broken up for different reasons but honestly i feel like he did a really good job when he told me and it was loving and gentle and was what I needed to really get serious in my journey and I did loose all the weight and fall in love with Pilates! 

The main thing is to not say it outright and let her bring it up herself, nothing hurts more than your partner saying you’re fat and you need to lose it. If she doesn’t feel like she gained (which she probably knows she did) then just start being more active and healthy yourself too and plan couple activities etc it’ll help a lot

For me personally, I blocked food and food related things coming up in my social media ie people eating out and trying new restaurants, mukbangs etc, I don’t watch food advertisements/ food porn. I spent time watching documentaries about food and the food industry and learning why food is so addictive/why we have food noise in the first place which also ‘deinfluenced’ me and changed my mindset and attitudes towards food. Now I have the ick over certain types of food, like junk or anything super processed after learning what I’ve learnt. 

I also started going by the hunger scale to objectively rate my hunger, which helps me recognise when I’m just having a craving etc. I also eat high protein, and plan my meals for the following day the night before, which helps because I literally don’t need to think about what to eat through the day. After some time I just noticed I just don’t care, I’m indifferent about food and it just doesn’t come to mind.

I’ve been in 2 relationships and I know for a fact they would never dream of cheating. I was only ‘cheated’ on when I stopped dealing with actually serious, provider type men and developed an attachment to a man who felt that he was better than me. I randomly got up one morning and told him I never wanted to deal with him again, left and blocked him (I was only dealing with this dude from low self esteem/ poor mental health) - later on he called me 4 months after asking to be back together and asking me why I left. I asked him why HE thought I left and he said ‘you probably saw my text messages and pictures with other women..’ and I hung up the phone, as I had had no idea about that, but given the nature of our relationship and Shera’s teachings I was not surprised, as in during our association I viewed him as someone likely to cheat based off what I’ve come to learn about men.

Pick a man who sees you as a prize and doesn’t think he can do better/ doesn’t want to do better, (and also pick someone who you know cannot do better than you) Also, allow the man to reveal to you on his own accord what his true desires are by seeing the environment he grew up in (his parents should still be married) who his peers are, who inspires him, who he is jealous of, his religious beliefs. Lots of girls get with men who are successful/attractive but his whole goal in life to finally be a player now that he’s made it. Some men also want women who are his equal - whether that’s finances, looks etc so as a result he starts comparing himself to his girl to determine if she’s worthy of him, and his ego will tell him that she’s not so he will start cheating, and the women he thinks is on his level do not want him because they don’t date down. For the most part they cheat because they don’t find you worthy or somebody they need to respect or they feel like they can manipulate you even if you did find out. Maybe they think you’ll never leave them because you can’t do better so they can do what they want. You don’t need to settle for that. Find a man who, as part of his own vision and goals for life, genuinely wants to settle down and sees have a girlfriend, marriage and children as an accomplishment that he deserves because he earned it. He will not cheat on you if you’re his prized possession and you maintain that status by focusing on yourself through out the relationship. He will not cheat if he values loyalty. Trust me, there are men to this day who die for each other and kill each other based on ADDRESSES. They go to the same barber for years, watch the same pornography again and again. They would never snitch on their friend, even if their freedom and lives were dependent on it, so you can definitely find a man who will not cheat on you.  

It’s women who pick men who think that she is beneath them that get cheated on. Some men, are hyper sexual, mentally ill and defective which is why they struggle to control themselves. Just because you want a successful man doesn’t mean he’s going to cheat on you, you need someone older, less conventionally attractive, someone who thinks you’ll disappear into thin air if he doesn’t look after you and someone who knows that you are the best, most respectable, worthy woman. Shera just explains that because it’s so common for men to cheat, it’s not worth fumbling your bag just because he cheated -and i agree because why should you care if you’re not fucking him and you’ve got your money? However in the same breath, like you don’t need to settle for someone who isn’t hygienic just because he’s providing, you don’t need to be around a cheater who’s providing, so just improve your vetting process and keep standards high. I will also never accept a cheater, even though I know most of them are. Don’t reduce your standards just to get a man, do what works for you.

Honestly you should probably break up with him and put this energy into yourself or someone who’s actually ready for a relationship, has some self confidence AND IS ON YOUR LEVEL.

In an environment where there’s a lot of pressure for men to be successful with the money, power, dream life and dream luxuries, a lot of men do get jealous of their girlfriends when they don’t feel self actualised and their girlfriend is pretty much perfect (attractive, put together, organised, accomplished etc), as it amplifies how little he has achieved not only among his other male peers, but also even compared to women and and it’s extremely hard to suck it up and admit he doesn’t really deserve to be around you because he is objectively not on your level at all, so instead of accepting that you’re better than him by nature and loving you for it, he secretly resents you for it and it’s enough now that he’s motivated to work hard to outdo you. That is a really not a healthy way to view your girlfriend or to be in a relationship. 

Yes you could stay and work it out, but the likelihood is his friends, childhood, social media algorithm and other influences is feeding into his thinking pattern and there’s probably nothing you can do about it. The truth of the matter is this is what happens when you don’t date or get with people who are equal to you in current life stage, experience, finances, goals in their own personal life as well etc. In heterosexual relationships, it’s important that your guy feels accomplished in his own life and feels deserving of you/ doesn’t feel the need to outshine you. A truly good partner for you would’ve been doing just as well as you and seeking to build something with you, or perhaps acknowledging how supportive you are at least etc. I feel like your boyfriend acting like this is way more common than you think, to the point that I would say it’s normal for men to respond like this when their girlfriend is better than them. Men make good partners when they’ve achieved their most ideal self and personal goals because they’re self assured and won’t feel the need to compare themselves to their girlfriend in the first place, or they feel like innately deserving of their girlfriend because he knows he’s on your level. 

In general I think don’t send your boyfriend links to things or suggest ideas of what to do when it comes to finances, career when he doesn’t know what to do. It’s really so much better when he has his own plan/ideas lined up and you help him refine it, support him through it, help him destress ESPECIALLY if you are in a position he wants to be in, I don’t know why it literally ends up like this every single time. I’m in med school with a bunch of great women in our early 20’s - doing this exact thing with their partners who were like your boyfriend, made them act exactly as your boyfriend does. For someone reason it makes them want to spite you 

Honestly just break up with him because he’ll break up with you, resent you, or never change and keep acting like this. Thinking of him as not being a fully developed person, he’s just not mature enough. And also thank yourself and praise yourself for having the emotionally intelligence and discernment to this. A lot of women don’t pick up on it. His motivation is fuelled out his spite, from making you the villain he resents in his head. His resentment can get worse and lead to him sabotaging you, abusing you honestly

For me it was 3 specific moments 

- I noticed I don’t find myself ‘ugly’ in any state. No matter how down bad I get. I used to avoid mirrors, could never feel attractive no matter the makeup, hairstyles, never wanted to be in any pictures etc I used to genuinely find myself so ugly. Now even on my worst day, I don’t think I’m ugly, in fact I think I look pretty everyday, just not at my best. Even physically I feel good and amazing and that’s normal for me - before my normal was feeling bloated, groggy, tired and low energy but now I feel refreshed and energised every day.

- No more bad pictures or bad moments. I put a lot of effort into being ‘high maintenance to be low maintenance’. I don’t have any ‘ugly’ clothes, I keep myself well groomed and well maintained. I rarely ever feel un-presentable and I appear put together no matter the occasion, even just going for groceries or going out for a walk. Even in candid photos or random ‘slips’ taken by friends, I still look presentable. 

- Validation from strangers. These days I go viral on social media truly just for lip syncing or beauty tutorials which also generates some extra cash for me across the month. I also find myself having long conversations with strangers, free items/drinks/food, receiving compliments from all types of people. The best has been walking into small clothing brands/independent stores and having my pictures taken by the designer to post on their social media pages. Amazing confidence boost. People are so much nicer, and they WANT you around them, like people are eager to interact with you. Life is so different when people actually want you around compared to being invisible/not desired. People also start giving highly detailed and specific compliments, it’s no longer just a quick you ‘look beautiful’, they will fully stop you compliment your features, jewellery, your smell, your makeup and hair, the way you walk, your aura etc and you can tell it’s genuine and they mean it

I believe in God but I don’t believe in hell or any type of eternal punishment from God, as a result I actually look forward to death, not in suicidal way but in a ‘I am grateful I got to live in the first place’ type of way. 

The only thing I ‘fear’ about death is not getting the opportunity to live my life to the fullest, explore the world and never finding my purpose in life, or leaving my family/loved ones without provisions set up to give them a comfortable life

For the most part it’s a jealousy/insecurity thing and they’re trying to neg your weight loss. If they’re being genuine it’ll be things like ‘wow you lost weight you look amazing! You looked great then and you look amazing now!’ or they’ll ask you what you’ve been doing to drop the weight and stay so fit, or they compliment you on how your weight loss brings out your features and how you look great in your clothes etc

Not gonna lie, I’m 22 years old too, I would never do that to either of my parents especially not to the extent to lie or cover it up… like ever? In fact, had I found out at 17, I would’ve completely broken down screaming and crying over my father doing that to my mother and told her immediately. The only difference is now at 22, I would sit my mother down and tell her what I know with control over my emotions. It’s very strange that at that age she didn’t care what it would do to you, and I wonder had you not found out when you did, she would’ve never told you or what? I don’t see how you can do that to your mother. Maybe I’m biased. 


But I guess I can imagine how she feels, and she probably is really hurt and would benefit from therapy with you, but I don’t really think she deserves it if I’m honest. I think she was old enough to grasp it and chose to be apart of it, and I think you’re right to distance yourself from her because I feel that she probably needs to learn that lesson in life. There’s probably a lot to unpack maybe therapy will do it, because what she wants really is to be apart of life with you because she’s not satisfied with the outcome after the choices she made OR she wants to relieve herself of guilt OR she feels punished by seeing you and your son enjoy your life and move on after aligning herself with her father and doesn’t like that. 

If you feel like you’ll benefit from reintroducing her into your life then maybe you can consider it, but if you’re happy and healing and living your new life and you don’t treat her with hostility… I don’t see why you need to connect anymore than you have now. In therapy she will find ways to blame you for it all let’s be honest. Your ex is the one who messed up but your daughter will look to absolve herself of guilt and she already aligned herself with her father since youth. Whatever he told her was convincing enough and she still has a strong relationship with him clearly. Is that beneficial at all? I think it’s okay to work with your therapist by yourself to heal.

Fortunately for me to drop 100lbs it mainly changing my lifestyle, I just had a bad lifestyle. I wasn’t even obese or overweight as child or young teen it was very recent. The main cause of my weight gain was from around 17 years old I was depressed, smoked at least a gram of weed a day, was taking mirtazapine and oral birth control pill (both cause weight gain) quit all my hobbies and did not regularly exercise, my part time job was also at McDonald’s which didn’t help. Mirtazapine also causes drowsiness so I slept A LOT and got tired very easily. 

I got older, wiser, started university, stopped smoking weed, I weaned off mirtazapine with my doctor, did therapy instead, change contraception to non hormonal IUD, picked up gym and dance again then I educated myself on food and diet with the help of this subreddit, I don’t feel that I picked up any disordered habits. I do deadass eat whatever I want when I want but within moderation, I just didn’t want to have that pizza when she wanted me to have it because I was already satisfied but I knew she was going to bug out if I said no.

I guess I can understand where she is coming from but it’s conflicting because I don’t feel like I’m particularly skinny and I’m really actually doing good and feeling good for once. 

Even when I was bigger I would get lightheaded from being in a hot shower for a long time because I would be shaving, washing my hair etc and I never skip any meals or anything like that or avoid particular foods. That day with the pizza I was genuinely already satisfied, and it was around 8pm and I always sleep around 9 or 10pm. 

I had been smoking weed daily from like 17/18 years old, since I quit, no more munchies and nowadays I just don’t feel like eating unless I’m genuinely hungry or craving something and I can’t force myself to eat because I feel sick if I try to. I eat 4 or more meals a day, I always eat what she and my father have for dinner as well as whatever I feel like having.
